text.title: Laravel Enterprise Patterns Examples
text.summary: Worked example: a greenfield POST /api/v1/orders slice applying the layering, validation, transaction and authorization rules end-to-end.

example.context: Laravel 11 API; `Order` model with an `OrderItem` child; POST /api/v1/orders accepts an items array; the write is transactional; Sanctum authentication.
example.walk: Step 1: artisan generates `Api\V1\OrderController` + `StoreOrderRequest` + `OrderResource` + `OrderPolicy`. Step 2: `StoreOrderRequest::rules()` returns ['items' => 'required|array|min:1', 'items.*.sku' => 'required|string', 'items.*.qty' => 'required|integer|min:1']; `authorize()` returns `$this->user()->can('create', Order::class)`. Step 3: `OrderService::create(array $data)` wraps the writes in `DB::transaction(...)`, creating the order and then its items, and dispatches notifications via `DB::afterCommit(...)`. Step 4: `OrderResource::toArray()` returns an explicit literal array — ['id', 'items' => OrderItemResource::collection($this->whenLoaded('items')), 'created_at'] — never `$this->toArray()`. Step 5: the controller method is four lines: `return new OrderResource($this->service->create($request->validated()));`. Step 6: `OrderPolicy::create()` returns `$user->subscribed()` and is registered in `AuthServiceProvider::$policies`.
example.output: Controller 32 lines; the transaction is scoped to the service; the Resource controls the API shape; authorization lives in the Policy; the layering audit script reports clean.

example.note: No Eloquent call, no transaction and no authorization branch in the controller — each lives in the layer that owns it.
